feijoo-cartas-eruditas-tomo-1-1773-spani:
After the Teatro Crítico, Benito Jerónimo Feijóo y Montenegro carried his work into letters. Tomo Primero of the Cartas Eruditas, y Curiosas gathers the first of them, in the 1773 edition, in Spanish. feijoo-cartas-eruditas-tomo-2-1773-spani:

feijoo-cartas-eruditas-tomo-3-1773-spani:

feijoo-cartas-eruditas-tomo-4-1773-spani:

The effect builds across the set: doubt used with care becomes a form of honesty. This volume shows that method still sharp in Feijóo's later years.
feijoo-cartas-eruditas-tomo-5-1773-spani:

feijoo-teatro-critico-tomo-1-1773-spanis:

feijoo-teatro-critico-tomo-3-1773-spanis:

feijoo-teatro-critico-tomo-4-1773-spanis:

feijoo-teatro-critico-tomo-6-1765-spanis:

feijoo-teatro-critico-tomo-7-1773-spanis:

the-kiltartan-poetry-book-prose-translat: Lady Gregory — the great patron of the Irish literary revival — renders Irish folk poetry into beautiful English prose. Songs and verses gathered around Kiltartan, in her native Galway, speak of love, exile, and the old gods. The collection helped the world hear Ireland's native voice, and it still sings.
the-memoirs-of-mr-charles-j-yellowplush: Thackeray's 1838 Memoirs of Mr. Charles J. Yellowplush: a footman's memoirs in his own spelling. The comic masterpiece of his youth, wildly funny. "Jeames" at his best, yellowplush's spelling is half the fun, thackeray's comic triumph.
the-paris-sketch-book-of-mr-m-a-titmarsh: Thackeray's Paris Sketch Book: the young satirist abroad. French manners mocked with English wit. The apprentice at play. Thackeray sketches Paris with a sharp pencil, the young satirist abroad, abroad, the young satirist abroad in France.
the-way-of-all-flesh: Samuel Butler held this novel back until after his death in 1902: the story of Ernest Pontifex, who breaks free from a crushing Victorian father. Drawn from Butler's own youth, it is wry, brave, and quietly furious. The book that freed the English novel from the paterfamilias.
tish: Mary Roberts Rinehart’s Tish leads a band of comic spinsters. Her escapades delight readers both young and old. Each tale is funny, warm, and very bright. A delightful collection for everyone to enjoy, comic.
